dispositions.topic_text: Acceptance and minimum representation guarantee for negative integers
dispositions.reason: The integer kind carries only OwnerRequest.stated_version and OwnerValues.upload_number, which are never negative; an object's floor is a text field of the project facts, read as text and checked by projects (A02), so a negative floor is carried as its text.

dispositions.topic_text: Public failure and redisplay behavior for invalid owner-form values
dispositions.reason: The texts already decide it: a form with a text its row's reads_as cannot read cannot be read; it is handed on with no values, no CSRF value and no credential and answered by the ordinary checks (State 5 owner surface, option (a) of round-51/55 T3).

dispositions.topic_text: Release-time enforcement of unique OWNER_FORM_FIELDS names
dispositions.what: Before a release is admitted, a check proves that no two rows of OWNER_FORM_FIELDS share a name. Options: check the source table in the specification checks; check the generated data provider constant; or both. Consequences: a source check catches it earliest, a generated-constant check also catches emitter faults, and both cost one more check. Every option must keep the guarantee that the name alone picks a row.
keeps:
No two rows share a name: the name alone
picks a row, and a table in which two rows share one is not a release.
No two rows share a name: the name alone picks a row, and a table in which two rows share one is not a release.
options: Validate uniqueness directly in the specification/data-table checker.
Validate uniqueness when generating the release constant.
Validate the generated release artefact before admission.
Check both the source table and the generated constant.
consequences: A source-table check rejects the defect earliest but does not independently detect a faulty projection.
A generation check protects the emitted constant but reports the defect later.
An admission check protects deployment while permitting invalid intermediate artefacts.
Checking both gives stronger coverage at the cost of duplicate validation logic.
